How to use African Playhouse

For families and friends who want to play African board and card games together, at one table or across countries, and for players who want to learn Songo, Oware, Fanorona or Morabaraba from clear rules.

Open African Playhouse ↗Platform detailsContact

Guided tourReal screens

Plays automatically. Use the dots or arrows to move, Pause to stop.

01

Getting started

1

Go to african-playhouse-staging.netlify.app.

2

The menu at the top switches the whole site between EN · English and FR · Français.

3

Open Games and pick a title marked Play now.

4

Choose Vs computer, Play Locally or Play Online, then the number of players.

5

Click Start a new game. The table is saved on the device.

6

To play with friends far away, choose Play Online, create a private room and send the invitation.

02

Features

01

The collection

24 titles sorted by family: board and strategy, dice and chance, puzzles, quick play, sowing and seeds, cards, dexterity. A filter shows only the 13 ready to play.

STEPS

  1. Search a game
  2. Filter by family
  3. Tick Ready to play
02

Ludo Afrique

Four colours, 2 to 4 players, computer opponents and table settings for house rules. The current game is saved on the device.

STEPS

  1. Roll with the space bar
  2. Pick a token with keys 1 to 4
  3. Change the table settings
03

Songo and Oware

Songo from Cameroon in the Nkul Beti edition: two rows of seven pits, 70 seeds, and the goal is 40 captured seeds, with a guided game and a rules and heritage page. Oware follows the Abapa edition: two rows of six pits, 48 seeds, 25 to win, with a learn and practice mode. Both have three computer levels.

STEPS

  1. Select a pit in your row
  2. Check where the seeds end
  3. Press Sow seeds
04

Naija Shapes

A card table inspired by Nigerian Whot: match a shape or a number, play special cards and empty your hand first. 2 to 6 players, against the House or with invited friends.

STEPS

  1. Choose the computer strength
  2. Pick the table convention
  3. Play a matching card
05

Private online tables

Create a private room, choose the game and the seats, and send a secure invitation. Ludo seats up to 4; Dames, Songo, Oware and Tic-Tac-Toe have two seats. A guest session needs no account or email. In this test version, online tables are for adults aged 18 or over.

STEPS

  1. Write your name at the table
  2. Create the private room
  3. Send the invitation
06

Traditions to come

Eleven more games are listed with their region, player count and estimated length: Bao, Yoté, Dara, Omweso, Shax, Seega, Senet, Ayo Olopon, Tsoro Yematatu, Shisima and Diketo. No release date is promised.

STEPS

  1. Open a title
  2. Read its region and rules
  3. See how friend play is planned
07

Atelier and Club

Boards, dice, tokens, avatars and themes to decorate your table. They are decoration only: every player has the same rules and dice odds. The Playhouse Club is proposed at 3.99 dollars a month and runs in test mode.

STEPS

  1. Browse the objects
  2. Preview a board or a die
  3. Select a free item
03Tips
  • Start Songo with the guided game before you face the computer.
  • In Settings, choose the language once for the whole site, and turn on high contrast or larger text if you need them.
  • Local games stay on the device. Save a free account to keep your friends across devices.
04FAQ
Do I need an account?

No. Solo and local games need no login and no payment. A free account keeps your friends across devices.

Can I play with family abroad?

Yes, at a private online table opened with an invitation. In this test version, online tables are for adults aged 18 or over.

Which rules are used?

Each traditional game names the edition it follows, such as Nkul Beti for Songo and Abapa for Oware, and shows its rules on the game page.

Do atelier items give an advantage?

No. They are decoration only. Rules and dice odds are the same for everyone.

Which languages?

English and French.
